criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
evidence: Purdue Campus GIS BuildingShapesZip4 identifies FID 197 as John W. Hicks Undergraduate Library at 504 Mitch Daniels Blvd.
The saved shell object HIKS_Exterior_Masonry_Walls has X/Y bounds matching the official polygon within 0.000026 m; 20 unique source vertices are within 0.000029 m of shell vertices.
limitations: The public GIS record is an official map polygon but is explicitly not a certified survey; it supports footprint, not wall section.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
evidence: The source polygon was independently transformed to the manifest local frame at placement origin [88.25, -317.24000549316406]; orientation and structural XY bounds match, with max vertex error 0.000029 m.
The sloped masonry loft’s upper perimeter is at Z=2.438 m and agrees with all 20 GIS points within 0.000623 m. The local asset bounds are plausible for its basement and roof forms.
limitations: The actual master Placement_hicks_library object was outside this asset-only review; no independent marker-placement error is claimed. The sloped apron lower-ring scale is estimated.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: Purdue GIS lists three levels and elevation attributes for ground floor, basement and roof/skylight; the model contains subterranean levels, roof deck, atrium and three pyramidal skylights.
The exterior reference supports the low square form and sloped masonry apron.
limitations: GIS metadata says these heights are unverified; it is not a surveyed elevation record. No measured section or full roof schedule was found. The roof/slab verticals, 2.438 m upper slope contact, skylight peak and basement topology remain provisional.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
evidence: The exterior photo shows the same low brick cube with broad sloped masonry walls; the asset models four GIS-perimeter lofted sloped faces.
Purdue’s 2013 renovation announcement/photo supports lounge banquettes, bistro tables, privacy screens, quick-access computers and an iDesk; the asset contains these categories.
limitations: The visible R2 render is schematic: the sloped brick reads pale/salmon compared with the darker red-brown exterior photo, entrance/exterior facade details remain sparse, and the interior has a limited camera view with uneven brightness. Furniture sizes and locations are interpretive rather than as-built.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: A separate Blender 5.2.3 LTS process freshly reopened the exact requested asset SHA; expected scene and exported collection exist, with 343 objects, assigned procedural materials, and no external image dependencies.
R2 evidence includes official GIS/photo/2013 renovation and master-plan sources, raw snapshots, renders, and explicit uncertainty notes.
limitations: The shared manifest currently caches object_count={next(a.get("object_count") for a in json.loads((ROOT/"modular/manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["assets"] if a["id"]=="hicks_library")}, while the actual export has {probe["object_count"]}; coordinator must refresh this count during integration.

findings: The official GIS footprint and upper sloped-wall perimeter are an exceptionally close match.
The visual form and documented furniture categories are represented, but wall slope, height, roof verticals and interior positions remain estimates.
Master integration should update the manifest object count; this does not change the exact asset grade.
limitations: No current public floor plan or dimensioned wall section was available.
The 2013 furnishing image documents the historical renovation, not current as-built furniture placement.
